issues: standard of review applicable to the IRB's credibility findings on appeal to the Federal Court — correctness or reasonableness
whether the tribunal is required to assess sur place risk arising from a public baptism in Canada independently of its finding that the claimant is not a genuine convert
whether a child's refugee claim must be assessed on its own risk factors rather than dismissed as purely derivative of the parent's claim
proper weight to be given to documentary evidence of religious conversion (baptismal certificate, pastor's letter) in a credibility assessment
whether a tribunal may rely on a religious-knowledge question (e.g. whether Jesus baptized people) to undermine the credibility of a conversion claim
independent risk to a child who witnessed the mother's public conversion and baptism in the country of origin
key_facts: claimant converted to Christianity in Iran and attended a house church
claimant was publicly baptized at a church in Canada while her daughter was present
first-level tribunal rejected both claims on credibility, finding the claimant was not a genuine convert
tribunal gave little weight to the baptismal certificate and pastor's letter
tribunal relied partly on a religious-knowledge question about whether Jesus baptized people
tribunal disposed of the child's claim as entirely derivative
no new evidence filed on appeal; oral hearing or rehearing requested
appeal argues no deference owed, sur place risk must be assessed regardless of sincerity, and child's risk requires separate analysis
causes_of_action: refugee protection claim (well-founded fear of persecution on the basis of religion)
sur place risk arising from public baptism in Canada
independent risk to a child from witnessing the mother's conversion
